input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: § 7.2 imposes the MFN on us, not on Vendor: we would have to extend to Vendor the best terms we offer any other technology supplier. It is unlimited as to product, term and comparison methodology, which is the rule's walk-away position rather than the fallback (a defined product, 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs). It also directly conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore delete § 7.2; nothing in the redline touches any MFN pricing granted by Vendor in our favour.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the open-ended obligation to give Vendor our best terms offered to any other technology supplier; our playbook does not accept MFN obligations running against the customer, and this clause also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Any MFN pricing granted by Vendor in our favour is unaffected.
